description: This topic explains how the body maintains a constant internal temperature through homeostasis and thermoregulation, focusing on the skin's role and the body's responses to heat and cold.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of homeostasis?

options.text: The breakdown of food to release energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment in the body
The movement of water into a cell
The transport of oxygen by the blood

mcq.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment such as constant temperature, water and sugar levels despite changes outside the body.

mcq.questionText: Thermoregulation refers to the control of which body condition?
mcq.explanation: Thermoregulation is the part of homeostasis that keeps body temperature constant.

mcq.questionText: Animals whose body temperature changes with the surrounding environment are called?
mcq.explanation: Ectotherms (poikilothermic animals) such as reptiles and fish have a body temperature that varies with the environment.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an endothermic animal?
mcq.explanation: A dog is a mammal and an endotherm that keeps its body temperature constant from internal heat, unlike the reptiles and amphibians listed.

mcq.questionText: Another name for endothermic animals is?
mcq.explanation: Endotherms are also called homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals because they keep a constant body temperature.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of the body is mainly responsible for regulating body temperature?
mcq.explanation: The skin contains sweat glands, blood vessels and hair that work together to control heat loss and gain.

mcq.questionText: When the body is too hot, sweat glands produce more sweat. How does sweating cool the body?

options.text: The sweat warms the skin surface
Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin
Sweat adds salt to the blood

mcq.explanation: As sweat evaporates from the skin it takes away heat (latent heat), cooling the body.

mcq.questionText: What happens to the blood vessels in the skin when the body is too hot?

options.text: They move deeper into the body

mcq.explanation: In heat, skin blood vessels widen (vasodilation) so more blood flows near the surface and more heat is lost.

mcq.questionText: Shivering helps to warm the body because muscle contractions?
mcq.explanation: Shivering is rapid muscle contraction that produces extra heat to warm the body when it is cold.

mcq.questionText: When the body is too cold, the skin's blood vessels respond by?
mcq.explanation: In cold conditions skin blood vessels narrow (vasoconstriction) so less blood reaches the surface and less heat is lost.

mcq.questionText: What is the approximate normal body temperature of a healthy human being?
mcq.explanation: The normal body temperature of humans is about 37 degrees Celsius.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important to keep body temperature constant?

options.text: So that enzymes can work at their best (optimum) rate
To stop the heart from beating

mcq.explanation: Enzymes that control body reactions work best at around 37 degrees Celsius, so a constant temperature keeps the body functioning properly.

mcq.questionText: In cold weather, hair on the skin stands upright. This helps the body by?

options.text: Trapping a layer of warm air close to the skin

mcq.explanation: Erect hairs trap a layer of air that acts as an insulator, reducing heat loss in cold conditions.

mcq.questionText: Which structures in the skin produce sweat?
mcq.explanation: Sweat glands in the dermis make sweat, which evaporates to cool the body.

mcq.questionText: A reptile is seen lying in the sun in the morning. This behaviour is best explained because reptiles?

options.text: Produce all their own body heat internally
Rely on the environment to raise their body temperature

mcq.explanation: Reptiles are ectotherms, so they bask in the sun to gain heat from the environment and raise their body temperature.

fib.questionText: The maintenance of a constant internal environment in the body is called _____.
fib.explanation: Homeostasis keeps conditions such as temperature, water and sugar steady inside the body.

fib.questionText: The regulation of body temperature is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Thermoregulation is the part of homeostasis dealing with body temperature.

fib.questionText: Animals whose body temperature varies with the environment are called _____.
fib.explanation: Ectotherms (poikilothermic animals) include fish, amphibians and reptiles.

fib.questionText: Warm-blooded animals that keep a constant body temperature are called _____.
fib.explanation: Endotherms (homeothermic animals) include birds and mammals.

fib.questionText: The main body organ responsible for temperature regulation is the _____.
fib.explanation: The skin uses sweat glands, blood vessels and hair to control body temperature.

fib.questionText: When the body is too hot, the skin blood vessels widen in a process called _____.
fib.explanation: Vasodilation brings more blood to the skin surface so more heat is lost.

fib.questionText: When the body is too cold, the skin blood vessels narrow in a process called _____.
fib.explanation: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin surface so less heat is lost.

fib.questionText: The cooling of the body when sweat changes from liquid to gas is due to _____.
fib.explanation: Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin and cools the body.

fib.questionText: Rapid contraction of muscles that produces heat in cold conditions is called _____.
fib.explanation: Shivering generates extra heat to warm the body when it is cold.

fib.questionText: The normal body temperature of a healthy human is about _____ degrees Celsius.
fib.explanation: Human body temperature is kept at around 37 degrees Celsius.

tf.questionText: Homeostasis means keeping the internal environment of the body constant.
tf.explanation: Homeostasis maintains stable internal conditions such as temperature and water levels.

tf.questionText: Reptiles are endothermic animals that produce all their heat internally.
tf.explanation: Reptiles are ectotherms; their body temperature depends on the environment.

tf.questionText: Birds and mammals are examples of homeothermic animals.
tf.explanation: Birds and mammals keep a constant body temperature, so they are homeotherms.

tf.questionText: Sweating helps to warm the body during cold weather.
tf.explanation: Sweating cools the body in hot conditions through evaporation; it does not warm it.

tf.questionText: During hot weather, the blood vessels in the skin become wider to lose more heat.
tf.explanation: Vasodilation increases blood flow to the surface so more heat escapes.

tf.questionText: Vasoconstriction increases the loss of heat from the body.
tf.explanation: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin surface, decreasing heat loss.

tf.questionText: Shivering produces heat through the rapid contraction of muscles.
tf.explanation: Muscle contractions during shivering release heat to warm the body.

tf.questionText: Maintaining a constant body temperature allows enzymes to work at their optimum rate.
tf.explanation: Enzymes function best at about 37 degrees Celsius, so constant temperature is important.

tf.questionText: The kidney is the main organ responsible for regulating body temperature.
tf.explanation: The skin, not the kidney, is the main organ of temperature regulation.

tf.questionText: When it is cold, hairs on the skin stand up to trap a layer of insulating air.
tf.explanation: Erect hairs trap warm air close to the skin, reducing heat loss.

hoq.questionText: A person walks from a cold air-conditioned room into the hot midday sun. Which combination of skin responses will most likely occur?
hoq.explanation: In hot conditions the body loses heat through vasodilation (wider skin vessels) and increased sweating which cools by evaporation.

hoq.questionText: Why does a lizard become slow and inactive on a cold morning but active during a hot afternoon?

options.text: It is an endotherm whose internal heat decreases at night
It is an ectotherm whose body temperature and activity depend on the surrounding heat
It sweats more in the cold than in the heat
It shivers in the afternoon to stay warm

hoq.explanation: As an ectotherm, the lizard's body temperature follows the environment, so it is sluggish when cold and active when warmed by the sun.

hoq.questionText: During a high fever, body temperature rises far above normal and may become dangerous. Why can a very high temperature harm the body?

options.text: It causes the skin to produce too much hair
It can denature enzymes so that vital chemical reactions stop working
It makes blood vessels disappear permanently

hoq.explanation: Very high temperatures denature (destroy the shape of) enzymes, so metabolic reactions slow or stop, which can be fatal.
